tasks.short: Write and install building energy-management routines

steps.what: Verify building-automation points, operating constraints, control authority and the intended energy-management sequence
Write energy management routines in the building-automation engineering category of {OTHER}, configuring native schedules, deadbands and reusable control blocks
Test the completed routine version against normal, fault and override cases; check exact target controller, point mapping, permitted window and rollback before installation
Install the exact checked energy-management routine on the checked building controller through the building-automation category of {OTHER}
Verify actual plant response after installation and decide whether failed acceptance conditions require the checked rollback; any rollback execution uses the separately gated installation step s4
Write and check the actual installed-version, test and commissioning record in {DOCS}
Save the exact checked commissioning record in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native scheduling and validated control-block reuse in the building-automation engineering category of {OTHER}. The authorised engineer checks the completed routine, target and rollback before a separate installation, then verifies actual plant behaviour and records the real outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated routine structure and point setup can be recreated manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native control blocks can reuse deterministic structure while keeping job-specific mapping explicit.
tasks.still_hard: Interlocks, occupied conditions and unintended plant interactions need engineering tests and observation.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer judges whether actual operation remains acceptable after a change.

ambition.what: No autonomous live control or expanded installation rights.

tasks.altitude: Less routine setup, unchanged responsibility for live changes.

reach.learn: Trace a software point to the actual sensor or actuator.

evidence.claim: Native control-block reuse can shorten routine setup but does not establish safe installed operation.

assumptions: Boundary is an already authorised energy-control change, excluding safety-system redesign and building operator labour. Existing change permissions remain; this scenario assumes the engineer has the stated installation authority.

The controls record supplies controller ID, point ID, unit, direction, limits and current version. The engineer verifies actual mapping and captures sequence, schedule and limits in s1-s2; missing mappings require manual tracing. Capture is counted, and runtime earns no saving.

Native configuration first. Shares are illustrative, not measured. Final s3 testing binds exact routine hash/version, target, window and rollback before installation; any change voids that check. Post-installation checks do not justify a pre-test approval.

s5 contains observation and the decision to invoke rollback, not an unlisted write action. Any rollback is a separate execution of s4 under the exact rollback version already checked in s3; its ordinary installation effort remains included in s4.
unknowns: Which routines already use native blocks
Existing installation authority and required plant acceptance tests
research_questions: What repeated authoring remains without touching plant safeguards?

already_counted.description: Routine authoring review, pre-install tests and actual plant verification remain in s2-s3 and s5.

incremental.description: Revalidate reusable control blocks after platform and plant changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact tested routine, target mapping, installation window and rollback version checked in s3; changes require retesting.
Actual commissioning record completed and checked in s6; edits void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Reusable routine setup saves 9 gross hours less 2 upkeep for 7 net. Already configured controls give zero gain. Mapping, testing, installation, observation and records retain effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Research renewable and alternative energy technology

steps.what: Find and read technical evidence about renewable or alternative energy systems, including solar thermal or photovoltaic options and their stated test conditions
Research technical applicability, resource assumptions, integration constraints, durability and limitations of the alternative energy technologies
Compare explicitly stated efficiency, output, area and cost assumptions in {SPREADSHEET}, using native unit and scenario formulas without equating unlike test conditions
Write and check the final research note, source conditions and uncertainty in {DOCS}
Save the exact checked technology research note in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native unit and scenario formulas in {SPREADSHEET} for explicit technology comparisons. Keep reading, applicability judgement and the final research note human, with source conditions visible beside each comparison.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated unit conversion and scenario arithmetic can distract from technical comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formulas can reuse arithmetic without claiming equal evidence quality.
tasks.still_hard: Laboratory output may not transfer to the actual resource, climate or building.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer judges which evidence is comparable and relevant.

ambition.what: No new investment or design approval authority.

tasks.altitude: Less unit arithmetic, unchanged research judgement.

reach.learn: Ask about maintainability and actual resource conditions.

evidence.claim: Explicit unit conversions can be configured deterministically; technology applicability is an engineering judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is research and a saved comparison note, excluding procurement and installation.

Publishers or suppliers provide technology, output, efficiency definition, test conditions, area, cost, date and source reference. The engineer checks and enters these during s1-s3; missing or incomparable values remain flagged and are investigated manually. No free structured supplier feed is assumed.
Native formulas first. Shares are illustrative and unmeasured. Final s4 checking follows completed comparison and note; changes invalidate its save gate.
research_questions: Which repeated arithmetic can be reused without hiding test-condition differences?

already_counted.description: Comparison checking and final research note remain in s3-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain formula tests and unit definitions.

approvals.approved_version: Final comparison and research note checked in s4; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeated arithmetic saves 5 gross hours less 1 upkeep for 4 net. Native formulas already present give zero gain. Source reading, applicability and final notes remain counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review and negotiate energy purchase agreements

steps.what: Review energy purchase agreements for volume, price basis, indexation, term, imbalance exposure, guarantees and exit provisions in {CLM}
Compare explicit price and demand scenarios in {SPREADSHEET}, retaining manual checking of contractual applicability and units
Negotiate energy purchase terms with the supplier within the existing mandate, discuss risks and clarify disputed provisions without executing an agreement
Write and check the final nonbinding negotiation note in {CLM}, including mandate limits, unresolved terms and exact supplier recipient
Save the exact checked negotiation note in {CLM}
Send the exact versioned nonbinding negotiation note to the checked supplier through {EMAIL}

tasks.design: Test native scenario formulas in {SPREADSHEET} using terms the engineer has actually read and checked in {CLM}. Keep interpretation and negotiation human; the completed nonbinding position is checked before its separate save and supplier send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Price formulas and demand scenarios can be repeatedly rebuilt.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit formulas can reuse arithmetic while preserving contractual assumptions.
tasks.still_hard: Risk allocation and ambiguous terms cannot be settled by numerical comparison.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer recognises an attractive headline price with unacceptable operating exposure.
tasks.altitude: Less scenario arithmetic, unchanged negotiating mandate.

reach.learn: Separate price comparison from binding acceptance.

evidence.claim: Explicit energy price and volume formulas can support scenarios without interpreting contractual meaning.

assumptions: Boundary is engineer review and nonbinding negotiation, excluding authorised contract execution, legal review and supplier labour. Existing mandate and specialist review remain; no free transferred work is assumed.

The supplier provides actual price basis, currency, unit, index reference, volume bands and effective dates. Demand records provide interval and quantity. The engineer verifies applicability and captures values in s1-s2; ambiguous clauses require manual clarification, not automated extraction or assumed defaults.

Native formulas first; illustrative shares are unmeasured. Final s4 check follows completed wording and binds nonbinding status, mandate and exact supplier recipient. Any edit voids both save and send approval.
unknowns: Limits of the engineer's negotiating mandate
research_questions: What repeated arithmetic remains after contract terms have been understood?

already_counted.description: Scenario review and final negotiating note remain in s2 and s4.

incremental.description: Maintain formula tests and changed index definitions.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final nonbinding negotiation note checked in s4; edits void approval.
Same note checked in s4 and saved unchanged in s5, to the supplier recipient checked in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeated price scenarios save 8 gross hours less 2 upkeep for 6 net. Existing formulas give no gain; contract reading, negotiation, actual note and actions retain effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult on sustainable building or renovation

steps.what: Review the construction or renovation brief, intended green-building framework and actual evidence supplied by the client or other engineers
Consult with construction or renovation clients and engineers on sustainable design, energy trade-offs and green-building requirements
Write and check the final consultation note in {DOCS}; reuse project and meeting headers while checking actual advice, limits and recipient
Save the exact checked consultation note in {DOCS}
Send the exact versioned consultation note to the checked client or engineer through {EMAIL}

tasks.design: Test native project-header reuse in {DOCS} for consultation notes. Keep sustainable-building interpretation and client discussion human, with actual advice checked in its final note before save and send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project identifiers and meeting details can be entered again in advice notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document fields can reuse existing headers.
tasks.still_hard: Certification frameworks, design trade-offs and project-specific evidence need interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer distinguishes possible design benefits from an unsupported certification promise.

ambition.what: No new certification or design approval rights.

tasks.altitude: A small note-formatting reduction; consulting judgement stays unchanged.

reach.task: Integrate energy constraints with renovation design
reach.learn: Explain energy trade-offs without claiming unverified certification credit.

evidence.claim: Native project fields can reduce consultation-note header entry while advice remains human-authored.

assumptions: Boundary is consultation and its ordinary note, excluding certification assessment, detailed design and client implementation.

The client supplies project ID, scope, framework and recipient. The engineer reads evidence in s1, obtains actual questions and advice in s2 and captures actual wording in s3. Missing context is clarified manually; no meeting transcript or prefilled advice is assumed.
Native fields first. Shares are illustrative and unmeasured. Ordinary final s3 checking follows completed advice and binds exact recipient; edits void both save and send checks.
unknowns: Whether project headers already populate natively
research_questions: Is repeated header entry real in actual consulting notes?

already_counted.description: Actual note writing and final advice and recipient checks remain in s3.

incremental.description: Maintain header mapping and template fields.

approvals.approved_version: Final consultation note checked in s3; edits void approval.
Same note checked in s3 and saved unchanged in s4, to the exact recipient checked in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Headers save 1.8 gross hours less 0.5 upkeep for 1.3 net. Existing header reuse gives zero benefit. Advice, reading, actual wording and save/send actions stay counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeated setup and arithmetic can shrink while plant changes, contracting and sustainable-building judgement retain human authority.
reach: Coordinate with controls technicians, procurement specialists and architects.
role.ambitious_version: An engineer who makes assumptions visible before changing a controller, recommending a technology or negotiating an energy term.

job.title: Energy Engineers, Except Wind and Solar
